system:
You are coding NSW motor accident decisions for a research dataset. Read the decision text supplied and assign each ordinal score from the text alone.

Score each dimension INDEPENDENTLY. A decision describing a severe case will score high on some dimensions and not others: severe physical injury does not by itself imply a contested proceeding, a disputed liability, or a prominent psychological component. Judge each scale against its own definition and resist letting an overall impression of severity carry across the scales.

If the text does not support a judgement on a dimension, give the lowest score rather than guessing upward, and say so in `uncertain`.

DECISION TEXT:
--- Catchwords ---
MOTOR ACCIDENTS -

Motor Accident Injuries Act 2017 ; settlement approval; pedestrian; injuries; right subtalar fracture requiring fusion in the future; psychological injuries; post-traumatic stress disorder; Held – proposed settlement in the sum of $520,000 approved; non-economic loss $330,000; past economic loss $40,000; buffer for future economic loss $150,000; settlement approved; complies with clause 7.37 of the Motor Accident Injuries Guidelines.

--- Key Paragraphs ---
[para 5] Records WPI threshold dispute then concession enabling non-economic loss.
5. The insurer initially relied on the opinion of Dr Keller dated 15 August 2023 to dispute the claimant's entitlement to non-economic loss. In a letter dated 23 August 2023 the insurer stated the claimant's whole person impairment did not exceed 10%. This position was ultimately altered and non-economic loss conceded having regard to the medical opinion of Dr Wines and the necessity for subtalar fusion surgery.

[para 13] Sets out the final agreed settlement breakdown including NEL, past EL, and future EL.
13. The insurer lodged an amended approval of settlement application and a further preliminary conference took place on 3 February 2026 with a settlement reached between the parties in the total sum of $520,000 representing non-economic loss of $330,000, past economic loss of $40,000 and future economic loss in the sum of $150,000.

[para 16] States the statutory approval framework under s 6.23 MAI Act and Guidelines.
16. Sections 6.23(2) and (3) of the Motor Accident Injuries Act 2017

(MAI Act) requires approval of the settlement and I am not to approve the settlement unless I am satisfied it complies with any of the requirements of the MAI Act or the Motor Accident Guidelines version 9.3 (Guidelines) commencing 4 December 2024.

[para 54] Notes the indexed statutory cap for non-economic loss relevant to proportionality.
54. The maximum that may be awarded for non-economic loss head of damage has been indexed since 1 October 2025 and the maximum is now the sum of $691,000.

[para 56] Cites proportionality principle and authority guiding NEL assessment.
56. The amount of non-economic loss damages to be awarded should be proportionate to the claimant's injuries and disabilities. In

RACQ Insurance Limited v Motor Accidents Authority of NSW (No 2) 2014 NSW SC1126. it was stated: 'It is a relationship of the award to the injury and its consequences... which is to be proportionate..... It is not a matter to be resolved by reference to some norm or standard supposedly to be derived from a consideration of amounts awarded in a number of other specific cases... The principle to be followed....It is that amount of damages must be fair and reasonable compensation for the injuries received and disabilities caused. It is to be proportionate to the situation of the claimant....and not to the situation of other parties in other actions, even if some similarity between their situations may be supposed to be seen. The judgement of a Court awarding damages is not to be overborne by what other minds have judged right and proper for other situations. It may be granted that a judge who is making such assessment will be aware of and give weight to current general ideas of fairness and moderation. But this general awareness is quite a different thing... The awareness must be a product of general experience and not formed ad hoc by a process of considering particular cases and endeavouring ... to allow for differences between the circumstances of other cases and the circumstances of the case in hand.' [Planet Fisheries Pty Ltd V La Rosa [1968] HCA 62 ; (1968) 119 CLR 118

per Barwick CJ, Kitto and Menzies JJ at paragraph 11].

[para 72] Finds the agreed past economic loss appropriate based on records.
72. I am satisfied that the calculations agreed upon accord with the actual losses sustained by the claimant as past economic loss. The sum of $40,000 inclusive of superannuation is appropriate. Future economic loss

[para 75] Accepts a future economic loss buffer due to surgery and impairment.
75. The insurer accepted there is ongoing impairment to the claimant's future earning capacity and allowed a buffer of $150,000.

[para 102] Applies s 6.23 and cl 7.37 criteria and recites the approved amounts and deductions.
102. Section 6.23 of the MAI Act provides the following restrictions on settling claims for damages:

(a) the settlement must be approved by a Member of the Commission and I am not to approve the settlement unless I am satisfied there is compliance with any of the requirements of the MAI Act or the Guidelines:

I am satisfied that there has been compliance with the Act and the Guidelines.

(b) The insurer to include in its application details of the following:

(i) the amount of the proposed settlement and a breakdown of the amount allowed for each head of damage:

the settlement is as follows – an amount for non economic loss in the sum of $330,000. The amount for past economic loss is $40,000 and future economic loss is a buffer of $150,000;

(ii) the amount of any deductions in the proposed settlement:

the insurer has made payments to the claimant by way of statutory weekly payments in the amount of $2,803.82. The insurer seeks credit. The claimant will received net proceeds of settlement in the sum of $517,196.18;

(iii) the amount of any advanced payments made be specified:

there had not been any advanced payments made, and

(iv) the evidence, documents and materials relevant to an assessment of the proposed settlement figure:

I have reviewed the clinical and medical records effectively convering the period of injury and the relevant period to date of this determination. I note the medical records accord with the claimant's reported symptoms, level of improvement and ongoing incapacity. The information produced by the insurer and the claimant has given me a good indication of the impact of injuries initially sustained, the recovery to date and the likely future treatment and prognosis.

(c) Clause 7.37 of the Guidelines, requires me to consider the following:

(i) the proposed settlement is just, fair and reasonable and within the range of likely potential damages assessments for the claim were the matter to be assessed by the Commission, taking into account the nature and extent of the claim and injuries, disabilities impairments and losses sustained by the claimant, and taking into account any proposed reductions or deductions in the proposed settlement:

Having reviewed the medical evidence produced in this matter, and the evidence of the claimant during the videolink conferences and her detailed written impact statement of some 15 pages in length, I am satisfied that the claimant continues to suffer some impairment to her lifestyle due to the ongoing problems with her right subtalar joint. It is being treated conservatively and will likely require surgery in the future. This has been taken into consideration when considering the sums agreed upon for non-economic loss of $330,000 and future economic loss of $150,000 consequent upon the likely subtalar fusion to be undertaken in the future. The amount for past economic loss of $40,000 accords with the factual basis of actual losses incurred. The claimant continues to suffer pain and restrictions due to the impact of her ankle injury. Her suffering continues and there is likelihood of considerable improvement in her symptoms with undertaking surgery by Dr Wines when her symptoms warrant it.

The allowances for past and future economic loss has been based on primary records produced to support the claimed losses. These losses accord with the most likely circumstances but for the accident.

I find the proposed settlement in the sum of $520,000 is just, fair and reasonable and within the range of likely potential damages assessments for the claim were the matter to be assessed by the Commission, taking into account the nature and extent of the claim and the injuries, disabilities, impairments and losses sustained by the claimant.

(ii) the claimant understands the nature and effect of the proposed settlement is the finality of her claim for damages and is willing to accept the proposed settlement:

The claimant was made aware during the many preliminary conferences that in the event she took the settlement, she could not seek any further damages for non-economic losses and economic losses.

The claimant is aware she will receive net proceeds of $517,196.18 with the deduction of $2,803.82 for weekly paymeents made to date.

I am satisfied that the claimant was aware of her rights and had freely agreed to the terms of settlement with an understanding of the settlement and its implications.

CONCLUSION

Assign each score:
  Injury Burden Intensity (0-4): overall physical burden of the injuries: 0 minimal, 4 catastrophic/multiple major injuries
  Treatment Burden (0-3): extent of treatment, surgery and ongoing care: 0 none or minimal, 3 extensive surgery and long-term care
  Work Impact Severity (0-3): loss of working capacity: 0 none, 3 total incapacity
  Legal Procedural Complexity (0-3): procedural complexity of the proceeding: 0 straightforward, 3 heavily contested
  Psychological Injury Emphasis (0-2): weight the decision gives to psychological injury: 0 none, 2 central
  Liability Clarity (0-2): how clear fault is: 0 seriously disputed, 2 clear or admitted
  Causation Complexity (0-2): difficulty attributing the condition to the accident: 0 straightforward, 2 heavily contested
  Pre-existing Condition Salience (0-2): how prominent a prior condition is in the decision: 0 absent, 2 central
